column2: How do I know what to do today and this week in my research?
column3: Add the “🗓 My research week” widget to the dashboard (or to the Follow-up page; it replaces the old “Daily work list”): everything waiting for you on a single list, the most urgent first — today’s and overdue reminders, letters without a reply (for how many days), upcoming archive visits, open leads and hypotheses, searches suggested by “What’s missing?” (including “search on SocFace”), what needs checking (SocFace readings, 🔴 / 🟠 alerts from the Database check), help requests, and what you did this week. On each line: ↗ to open it, ✓ when it is done, ⏭ to postpone to tomorrow or next week (“↶ Undo” at the bottom left). ✎ to choose “Today” or “This week”, sort by urgency or by kind, hide or reorder the kinds and the number of lines; ⛶ to see everything in large.

column2: Which records should I look for first?
column3: Add the “💡 Research suggestions” widget to the dashboard: the gaps in your Sosa line (birth, marriage, death, unknown parents), with the place and the years to search, the closest generations first.

column2: Where can I see the history of a village?
column3: Lists → Village record: the families, the occupations, the church, the population over the censuses and the Cassini map. ⚙️ “Organise the record” arranges, hides or widens each part; the census plan and a notepad are there too.

column2: How do I hide, arrange or add columns in a list?
column3: In all the table lists of the Lists tab, the “⚙️ Columns” button.

column2: How do I see the anniversaries to celebrate (Dates to celebrate)?
column3: Dashboard → “🎂 Dates to celebrate” widget (the former “Today’s anniversaries”): today, this week or this month. Living people with their age (“Marie is 40”), ancestors “150 years ago”; round anniversaries are highlighted (🎉, golden wedding…). Filters All, Living, Ancestors, ⭐ Sosa; with the pencil ✎: a single branch, only births, marriages or deaths, only round anniversaries. 🔔 on a line sets a reminder (the day before, a week before or on the day) in Lists → Reminders. Confidential records are never there; in view-only mode 🔒, a living person appears only by their first name.

column2: How do I file an old postcard and find it on the map?
column3: Lists → “🏞 Postcards” → “＋ New postcard”: the front (the view) and the back (the written side), the publisher, the number, the date sent, the postmark, who wrote it and to whom, the address, the text on the back (“📜 Transcribe in the workshop” for the image of the back), the place shown and, if you like, the direction of the view. The cards in your media sent as “front/back” are already there, marked “To complete”. On the Map, the “🏞 Postcards” button shows them at their location, with a cone for the direction; the place’s page (Municipality monograph) and a village record have a “🏞 Postcards” block.

column2: How do I say where an old photo or a postcard was taken, when I am not sure?
column3: Open the image (viewer) → “📍 Where was it taken?”, or Lists → “📍 Images of places” → “＋ Add an image”. Add one or more hypotheses: a place in your database (picker), a precise point on the map, or an area (◯ circle or ⬠ polygon) if you only know the neighbourhood; the street and the address; the direction of the view (🧭, a cone on the map); the certainty (certain, probable, possible, to check) and why (shop sign, bell tower, caption, publisher…). The ★ hypothesis chosen becomes the image’s place everywhere in the app. Also note the date the picture was taken (“about 1905”) and the publisher or photographer.

column2: How do I compare an old postcard with the same place today?
column3: In “📍 Where was it taken?” → “🪟 Compare with today”: choose or import a current photo taken from the same spot. The comparer opens as a curtain (drag the line in the middle of the image) or as a cross-fade. “📌 Place 2 markers per photo” (the top of the bell tower, the corner of a roof) aligns today’s photo with the old one; “Adjust by hand” rotates and enlarges it, and “Drag moves photo B”. “💾 Save” keeps the comparison.

column2: How do I ask for help to locate an old photo?
column3: In “📍 Where was it taken?” → “🙋 Ask for help”: the app prepares the text (what can be seen, your leads with their certainty, your questions), to copy onto a forum, Geneanet’s mutual help, a Facebook group (the request is stored in Lists → 🤝 Help requests), or a small ad (stored in ✉️ Small ads). “⤓ Download the image” to attach it. When someone answers, “📨 Note an answer”: their lead becomes a new hypothesis, with their name (↶ Undo possible). Nothing is sent by the app.

column2: Where can I see the old images of a street or a village?
column3: A village record and a municipality monograph have an “🖼 Images of the place” block: the images arranged by street, then by period, with the map (areas and directions of view). Lists → “📍 Images of places” also sorts them “By street” or “By period”, with the filters Place, Street, Period, Certainty, Kind, No place. On the Map, the “📍 Images of places” button shows them at their location.

column2: How do I note my appointments and family birthdays?
column3: Lists → My diary: fairs, archive visits, reminders, letters, tours, by day, by week, by month… Lists → Family calendar: the events of the records by day, by month or by year, with an “anniversaries” mode and the date in other calendars (Julian, Republican…).

column2: How do I make a map with my photos and videos?
column3: Lists → “Photo maps” → “＋ New map” (or Maps → “📸 Photo maps” mode: at the top, one badge per map to go from one to another, “🗺 All my maps” and “＋ New map”; the ⚙️ button next to them chooses which ones get a badge: the most recent, the oldest (with their number) or those you pick by hand; the others are in “🔍 N other maps…”, which opens the search). Add photos from the app (“＋ Photos from the app”) or drag files into the “📁 Drag…” area: they go into the media, and those with GPS coordinates (JPEG, HEIC, PNG, WebP photos, MP4 and MOV phone videos) place themselves. The others go into “To place”: drag their thumbnail onto the map, or 📍 to choose a place from your database.

column2: A photo is in the wrong place on my photo map, how do I fix it?
column3: Drag its thumbnail to the right place: “↶ Undo” appears at the bottom left. The original GPS position is kept: ✎ (or right-click the thumbnail) → “↺ Back to GPS”. Several photos in the same place form a cluster with their number: click it (or zoom) to separate them.

column2: How do I see my photos over time on the map?
column3: Under the map, the timeline shows how many photos there are per period (wheel to zoom: from centuries down to minutes; double-click to see everything). Drag on the timeline to choose a period. “▶ Play” fills the map over time; ⏮ ⏭ step forward. The step is typed freely: “3 d”, “1 month 12 d 3 h”, “2 years 6 months”, “90 min” (or the quick choices 1 h, 1 d, 1 wk, 1 month, 1 year, 10 years); the window is cumulative (everything before stays) or sliding. The exact time of a photo (read from the file, or written “7 May 1925 at 14:30”) is the local time it was taken; a date without a time is placed at noon.

column2: Can I combine all my photo maps?
column3: Yes: “🗺 All my maps” (in Lists → Photo maps, or in Maps). Each map has its colour; the legend on the right lets you tick and untick the maps, with the same filters (📷 Photos / 🎬 Videos, period, timeline). The “📸 Photo map” widget can also go on the dashboard, in your tabs and in a note.

column2: How do I put the record of a specific village in a widget or a tab?
column3: Widget editor (kind “App screen”) or Tab editor: “Village record…” or “Municipality monograph…” screen, then the commune. Tick the parts to show and arrange them (⠿ or ↑ ↓): this organisation only applies there, the village record in Lists keeps its own.

column2: A place is in the wrong spot on the map, what should I do?
column3: Settings → ✅ Database check, “📍 Places” badge: the app spots unlikely coordinates (0, 0, outside the country, latitude and longitude swapped, namesake in another department), shows the map above the list and offers “✎ Fix” in one click (with “↶ Undo”).

column2: How do I choose an icon or a base map when there are lots of choices?
column3: Click “✎ Change” next to the icon (or the background): a grid opens. Type a word in the 🔍 box (“church”, “boat”, “heart”, “Cassini”…), or click a section at the top; your recent icons come first. The keyboard arrows move around the grid, Enter chooses, Esc closes. For base maps, each thumbnail shows a piece of the background. The “×” of the badge removes the icon when you can do without it. It is the same grid everywhere: event types, base maps, icons of sections, tabs, widgets, the big buttons of simple mode, notes…

column2: How do I find a setting in a long Settings page?
column3: The long Settings pages (Keyboard shortcuts, Event types, Appearance, Glossary…) have a 🔍 box just under the title, which stays at the top when you scroll. Type a word (“sosa”, “print”) or a key (“ctrl p”): only the lines that contain it stay, the letters found are highlighted, the frames without a result fold up into a grey line. “/” puts the cursor in the box, Esc or × empties it, “Show all” brings everything back. Nothing found? “🔍 Search all Settings” takes the word to the box in the left column.

column2: How do I change the base map?
column3: Map → map settings: Cassini, État-Major, IGN, satellite, old cadastre… A village record also has its own choice.

column2: How long did it take to go from one village to another in the old days?
column3: Map → “🧭 Tools ▾” → “Distances and travel times”: choose the start and the destination (or a person, to follow their movements) and the year. You see the distance and the duration on foot, on horseback, by stagecoach, by boat and by train, with a sentence like “It took about 4 days to go from Tulle to Paris in 1820”. The speeds come from historians (Braudel, Arbellot, Studeny, Caron…): the sources are in “⚙️ Speeds and sources”, where you can also change them. On the record, the “🧭 Their journeys” block appears as soon as the person lived in two places placed on the map.

column2: How do I print a large family map (A3, A2, A1, A0)?
column3: Map → “🧭 Tools ▾” → “Large map to print”: format A3 to A0, portrait or landscape, 5 styles (old, État-Major, modern, black and white, midnight blue and gold), cartouche (title, family, dates), legend, compass rose, scale, places of birth, marriage and death, migrations, a single branch, portraits in medallions. “⤓ Export…” gives a PDF, a PNG, a JPG or an SVG; “🖨 Print” opens the print window. Living people and confidential records are never on it. The background is drawn by the app (Natural Earth, IGN), without Internet tiles: their terms of use forbid downloading them in bulk for printing, and a drawing stays sharp at every size.
